title: Approve the admin overview composition
question: These three comps use the admin index direction you selected. Which one should be the build reference? What should carry forward, what feels false, and should it be approved, combined, revised, or rejected?

options.label: Three-column operations index
options.lineage: A precise design-annual index with three equal operational sections
options.thesis: A disciplined index makes Tenant, Support, and Provider health easy to scan.
options.viewport: A compact horizontal nav sits above three equal columns; each section shows an explicit unavailable state until connected data exists.
options.risk: Equal panels may understate the different depth of tenant, support, and provider workflows.

options.label: Stacked operations index
options.lineage: The same editorial index, arranged as three horizontal rows
options.thesis: A vertical list keeps every operational area readable at full width.
options.viewport: Tenant, Support, and Provider health each occupy an equal horizontal row with the label left and unavailable state right.
options.risk: Stacked rows use more page height as real data becomes available.

options.label: Side-rail operations index
options.lineage: The selected editorial index with persistent vertical application navigation
options.thesis: A side rail keeps operational sections within reach while preserving the three-way overview.
options.viewport: A narrow navigation rail anchors the shell; the main area retains three equal unavailable-state panels.
options.risk: A persistent rail reduces the width available to the overview at laptop sizes.
